title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing from the previous page): T̃ → T is a functor of groupoids, here the passage between Teichmüller groupoids. It behaves like a fibration or cofibration in groupoids, with fibre groupoids T̃_s (written C̃_s). Grothendieck wants a presentation of the total groupoid T̃ by generators and relations, built from three ingredients:

(i) A presentation of the base T. Its generators u_i have relations (8), each a closed composable word u_{i'_{α,1}} … u_{i'_{α,n_α}} = 1.
(ii) Chosen lifts ũ'_i of the u_i.
(iii) A family of 'fibre arrows' a_j. In each fibre these generate the fibre groupoid; in particular every vertex is a source or target of some a_j.

Previous page. A base relation (8) is lifted step by step. Between consecutive lifted arrows, the endpoint t̃_{i_k} and the next start point s̃_{i_{k-1}} lie over the same object. Assuming they lie in the same connected component of the fibre, one joins them by a fibre word M_{α,k}((a_j)). This gives the composable chain (11).

This page.
- The composite of (11) maps to an identity in the base, so it lies in a fibre groupoid.
- Since the a_j generate that fibre, it can be written as a word in the a_j. Equivalently, one chooses a closing word M_{α,1}((a_j)): t̃_{i_1} ⇝ s̃_{i_n} so that the whole loop is the identity. This gives relation (12): M_{α,1} u'_{i'_{α,1}} M_{α,2} u'_{i'_{α,2}} ⋯ M_{α,n_α} u'_{i'_{α,n_α}} = 1. It is the lifted ('remontée') form of base relation (8).
- Next one takes a family of relations (13) N'_β((a_j)) = 1 among the fibre arrows. Those relations living in a fixed fibre C̃_s are required to give a presentation of C̃_s on the generators a_j.
- One further hypothesis is that, at each vertex s̃, the a_j with target s̃ form a generating system (continued on the next page).

Next page. One adds transport relations (14): ũ_i(a_{j0}) = M''_{i,j}((a_j)). These express how a lifted base generator conjugates or transports each fibre generator based at its source into a word in the fibre generators. The claim is that (12)+(13)+(14) present T̃.

Modern reading: this is the groupoid/fibred version of the classical presentation of a group extension (P. Hall's lemma; Johnson's 'Presentations of groups'). Generators are fibre generators plus lifts of base generators. Relations are:
- fibre relations;
- lifted base relations, corrected by fibre words;
- conjugation (action) relations.

In context it is a tool for computing presentations of Teichmüller groupoids T_{g,ν} inductively along forgetful or Birman-type fibrations. This serves the Esquisse programme of describing the Teichmüller tower by generators of low modular dimension and relations of dimension ≤ 3.
errors: Notation slips. The transcription's S̃_{i_n}, T̃_{i_1} should be lower-case s̃, t̃. The indexing of the M_{α,k} is inconsistent: M_{α,1} is used for the closing word t̃_{i_1} ⇝ s̃_{i_n}, but elsewhere M_{α,i'_{α,n_α}} appears.

Implicit hypotheses must be made explicit for the lemma to hold. Consecutive endpoints must lie in the same connected component of the fibre; Grothendieck states this on the previous page. T̃ → T must have the transport (cofibration-like) property for (14) to make sense. The (12) relations need to be imposed for every lift choice, or else the result must be shown independent of choices; this is a standard but nontrivial check left implicit.

ideas.what: Presentation of a total groupoid fibred over a groupoid. Generators: fibre generators plus lifts of base generators. Relations: fibre relations, lifted base relations closed by fibre words, and transport/conjugation relations.
ideas.modern_name: Presentation of a group extension / of a Grothendieck construction of groupoids (Hall's lemma for extensions; groupoid version in Brown–Higgins style)
ideas.usually_credited_to: P. Hall (group extensions); standard in combinatorial group theory (D.L. Johnson); groupoid versions in R. Brown, P.J. Higgins
ideas.where_published: Not as such. Esquisse d'un programme only states the resulting philosophy for the Teichmüller tower.

ideas.what: Using such a fibration lemma to obtain presentations of Teichmüller groupoids inductively along forgetful maps between levels.
ideas.modern_name: Birman exact sequence method for mapping class group / Teichmüller tower presentations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birman; Hatcher–Thurston, Wajnryb, Gervais; Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (Teichmüller tower); Bakalov–Kirillov
ideas.where_published: Spirit in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §2-3, without this lemma.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but standard groupoid version of the presentation-of-extensions lemma, used as a technical step toward presenting Teichmüller groupoids. It is interesting as evidence of Grothendieck's working method, but contains no new result or unexplored connection.
transcription_corrections: Margin note next to (12) reads 'relation (8) "remontée"' (the lifted relation (8)), not 'relation "commutation" (8)'.
S̃_{i_n} → T̃_{i_1} should read s̃_{i_n} → t̃_{i_1}.
Insertion above the line reads roughly 'à flèches génératrices … dans …' (inserted remark about generating arrows of the fibre).
'relatives : une catégorie-fibre' should read 'relatives à une catégorie-fibre fixée C̃_s, soient définissantes pour celle-ci (familles génératrices de flèches (a_j))'.
Last line: 'les flèches a_j qui ont leur but en s̃ forment une' rather than 'qui sont des buts en s̃'.
